disposition_reason: The paper has an ordered neural-decoding R-squared endpoint, but exact regional baseline values and the paper-compatible runtime are unrecovered. Pinned generic author defaults and the local evaluator differ from journal cohort, folds and aggregation; significant regions or a mouse-held-out extension cannot substitute.

source_paper.title: Brain-wide representations of prior information in mouse decision-making

evidence.locator: Methods: Inclusion criteria; Electrophysiology data; WFI data; Nested cross-validation; Assessing statistical significance
evidence.supports: Original modalities, cohort counts, feature windows, nested folds and corrected-score aggregation.

evidence.locator: significance_by_region; argument defaults; regional output construction
evidence.supports: Generic script uses median scores minus median null medians and at least two sessions, unlike the paper methods.
Registered task includes neural/movement prior decoding. Local component explicitly names generic script defaults, lists paper conflicts and reports zero authentic runs.

target.description: Decode the Bayes-optimal prior from pre-stimulus neural activity; retain movement-predictor and pseudosession controls. Better prior decoding does not prove causal prior computation.

dataset.description: Paper identifies the 2024 IBL release and separate WFI recordings; registration pins the 2023_12_bwm_release loader family. Exact versioned input manifest and modality coverage are not yet reconciled.

cohort.description: Journal regional analyses contain 414 Ephys sessions/242 regions/2,289 region-sessions and 51 WFI sessions/32 regions/1,539 region-sessions. The exact roster must be recovered, including the separate 171-session movement subset.

split.description: Ephys uses nested interleaved fivefold outer and fivefold inner trial CV; WFI uses 50 outer folds and leave-one-out inner CV. Ten random splits are repeated. New held-mouse/session testing changes the original task.

inputs.description: Ephys binned spike counts and WFI pixel fluorescence are modality-specific inputs; behavior/video predictors are controls, not extra oracle information for the neural decoder.

preprocessing.description: Ephys sums spikes from -600 to -100 ms and uses Lasso; WFI uses frame -2 and Ridge. Preserve published QC, reaction-time and minimum-trial/unit/pixel inclusion.

metric.description: R-squared measures prior decoding; corrected R-squared subtracts the median of 1,000 pseudosession scores. Counts of significant regions and smaller p-values do not measure prediction improvement.

aggregation.description: Paper takes median R-squared over ten repeats, then mean session corrected R-squared per region. Pinned stage3 instead takes median score minus median null medians and requires two sessions; reconcile the actual publication pipeline.

comparison.primary_metric: Source-paper pre-stimulus Bayes-optimal-prior decoding R-squared and regional null-corrected R-squared

published_baseline.description: The paper reports regional decoding plots and related statistics, but an exact publication-linked regional score vector and a source-defined overall improvement scalar were not recovered.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: No journal-compatible author rerun is established; the installed evaluator only checks generic pinned-script semantics.

minimum_effect.rationale: Define practically meaningful corrected-R-squared gain on the original complete region/modality panel after recovering baseline variability; do not substitute more significant regions.

uncertainty.method: Unresolved: use paired original-task score differences with animal-level dependence and declared region/modality multiplicity; determine a valid rule before evaluation.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Mouse, retaining repeated sessions and regions within mouse; WFI and Ephys populations remain separate.
uncertainty.rationale: Trial folds, regions and repeated sessions are dependent. Pseudosession significance controls drift-related nulls but is not uncertainty for candidate-minus-author improvement.

paper_win_requires: Recover publication-linked numeric baseline scores and resolve all paper-versus-script configuration conflicts.
Use the original modality-specific inputs, windows, inclusion rules, prior target, trial splits and score aggregation for the complete declared source panel.
Retain movement/pseudosession controls; do not reward significance or anatomical coverage as if it were higher predictive performance.
Report new mouse-held-out/session-held-out testing only as an extension, and predeclare meaningful effect and valid paired uncertainty before final scoring.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison was source-verified; paper and rerun baselines are separate.

episode.improvement_loop: Source recovery blocks admission. Future iteration uses training/inner-validation folds under the original modality-specific protocol, with explicit public-target exposure accounting.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze preprocessing, prior construction, candidate, feature policy and search configuration before protected outer-fold scoring.
episode.final_evaluation: Score on exact original trial partitions and source cohort, preserving ten-run and null corrections; do not use generic-default reconstruction as a paper-win decision.
episode.baseline_policy: Published regional results, a journal-compatible author rerun and generic-script reconstruction are distinct comparators. No local authored baseline replaces the source.

blocking_issues: Exact source baseline score vector and source-authorized overall comparison rule are missing.
Original input roster/version and exact fold identities are not bound.
Paper-versus-script conflicts include estimator/folds, run and regional aggregation, null count, session/unit filters and reaction-time limit.
No complete same-task evaluator, uncertainty/effect rule or concrete episode budgets are admitted.

legacy.notes: Preserve the generic-script initial evaluator and historical definition for calibration. Its run-mean, 200-null, 50-fold script protocol and Fisher/BH output are not a journal reconstruction or scientific success criterion.
